# FCR Breakout Room – Kickoff Call  
**Date:** January 20, 2026  
**Time:** 14:00 UTC  
**First session of the Fast Confirmation Rule (FCR) breakout room**

### Resources
- **Zoom link**: https://ethereumfoundation.zoom.us/j/4840114962?pwd=S8FArsXkTutjZDmVohZ7b0VOCaY4An.1
- **Facilitator email**: [will@ethereum.org](mailto:will@ethereum.org)
- **Facilitator Telegram**: @corcoranwill

### Agenda Overview
This inaugural call focuses on **high-level overviews**, **expectation setting**, and **community alignment** for the Fast Confirmation Rule initiative.

Key topics:
- Introduction to FCR and its goals  
- Walkthrough of the current consensus-specs PR [#4747](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4747)  
- Presentation from core researchers (including @mkalinin )  
- Scheduling cadence & contribution expectations  
- Team introductions & open Q&A  

**What is FCR?**  
FCR is an **opt-in**, out-of-protocol upgrade that enables near-instant Ethereum transaction confirmations (~12–24 seconds) by iteratively determining a “confirmed” block at the start of each slot using real-time validator attestations and LMD-GHOST scoring — **no hard fork required**. 

We’ll leave plenty of time for questions and discussion.

**Looking forward to seeing everyone there!** 🚀  
Feel free to reply with any agenda suggestions in advance.

comments.body:
Hi, I am on leave until the end of the week so I will likely miss today’s call. Here is a quick summary on our end.

* We have implemented the earlier version of fast confirmation in our fast-confirmation branch. Some writeups and results are here https://ethresear.ch/t/fast-confirmation-rule-on-safe-head-in-prysm/22167
* We have been testing the branch internally. It works as expected, but there are a few bugs to sort out and it still needs a thorough audit. This has slowed down since I have been more focused on epbs and gloas
* I have studied the latest fast confirmation spec and raised a few questions on telegram channel, in particular around how difficult it would be to track unrealized justified state. In Prysm and likely other clients, tracking a new state like this is not trivial, so whether this can be avoided still needs more study. This is the biggest blocker for updating our implementation to the latest spec
* I have a branch for the latest fast confirmation spec, but it is not complete, roughly 25 percent done. I can focus on this after my leave if we think it is a high priority
Linking slides from Luca and Mikhail https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1zMLroOCxJIgAUFuQdcG3FRcDz_7ZC4Ja7-yxO0z5S_c/edit?usp=sharing
